concepts.heading: Read the Event's Rules
concepts.plain: Every event has its own rules. Read them before you go and follow them there.

concepts.heading: Talk With Partners First
concepts.plain: Agree beforehand what each of you is and isn't open to, and how you'll check in.

concepts.heading: Plan Your Night
concepts.plain: Arrange your way home, bring what you need, and keep alcohol low or none.

checks.prompt: Two partners disagree in the middle of a party about what's OK. What would have helped most?
options: Deciding on the spot without the other partner
Agreeing on limits and check-ins before going
checks.explanation: Talking about limits and check-ins beforehand prevents hard negotiations in a busy, distracting place.

4c105af6-8f28-547c-b2c1-5781ced4e878.takeaway: Read the rules, make your plans and agreements ahead of time, and arrive clear-headed.

concepts.heading: Ask Before Any Touch
concepts.plain: Always ask before touching anyone, even a hug, and even if you've touched before.

concepts.heading: Ask Each Person Separately
concepts.plain: When approaching a couple or group, every person decides for themselves.

concepts.heading: No Means No, and Maybe Means No
concepts.plain: Accept a no, a maybe or silence the first time, without arguing or asking again later.

concepts.heading: Watching Needs Consent Too
concepts.plain: Ask before joining or watching a scene, and follow the event's rules about watching.

checks.prompt: Taylor asks a couple to join them, and one partner says "Sure, we're both in." What should Taylor do?
options: Go ahead, since one partner agreed for both
checks.explanation: Each person consents for themselves. Taylor should hear a yes from the other partner too.

checks.prompt: You see a scene you'd like to join. What is the right move?
options: Join in quietly so you don't interrupt
Stand very close to get noticed
Wait for a natural pause and ask, or don't join at all
checks.explanation: Joining without asking breaks consent. Ask at an appropriate moment, and accept the answer.

209cd450-fbc3-52c2-88b6-69d7b7a95cf8.takeaway: Ask every person, every time, and take any no or hesitation as a no.

concepts.heading: No Photos Without Permission
concepts.plain: Never take or share photos or videos of people without their clear permission.

concepts.heading: Don't Out Anyone
concepts.plain: Who you saw and what they did stays private. Seeing someone there doesn't give you the right to share it.

concepts.heading: Respect Everyone's Space
concepts.plain: Use the names people give, don't hover, and welcome newcomers.

checks.prompt: Sam sees a coworker at an event. What should Sam do?
options: Mention it at work so things aren't awkward
Keep it private and follow the coworker's lead
checks.explanation: Who attends an event is private. Sam should keep it to themselves.

d329801e-7722-5fec-b69f-e107eb362fd2.takeaway: No photos, no outing anyone, and treat everyone as you'd want to be treated.

concepts.heading: Tell the Hosts
concepts.plain: If someone breaks consent or makes you uneasy, tell a host or the consent team.

concepts.heading: Look Out for Each Other
concepts.plain: Check on friends who seem unwell or overwhelmed, and get help if needed.

concepts.heading: Leaving Early Is Fine
concepts.plain: You can leave at any time, for any reason, and you don't owe an explanation.

concepts.heading: Check In Afterward
concepts.plain: Talk with partners the next day about what went well and what to change.

checks.prompt: You notice someone ignoring another guest's no. What should you do?
options: Tell a host or the consent team
checks.explanation: Hosts and consent teams can act straight away. Telling them protects everyone.

checks.prompt: After a party, one partner feels unsettled. What helps most?
options: Ignore it, since the party is over
Blame the other partner for going
Talk it through with care and decide what to change next time
checks.explanation: A caring check-in after an event helps partners process feelings and improve next time.

125d74a8-af58-5555-a078-e68f7d38ce70.takeaway: Speak up to the hosts, look out for each other, and check in after.
